title: Fossils Show an Early Human Relative Lived in Africa Very Long Ago
summary:
Scientists have studied new fossils from a cave in South Africa. They say an early human relative called Homo erectus lived there about 2 million years ago. That is about 200,000 years earlier than many scientists used to think.

Homo erectus belongs to the same group as modern humans, called Homo. It is probably one of our direct ancestors.

The fossils come from a cave called Drimolen, in an area known as the Cradle of Humankind. Many fossils from the cave had never been studied closely. A team led by La Trobe University in Australia looked at 18 of them.

One fossil is part of an adult Homo erectus skull. Before, scientists only had a child's skull from this cave.

Another relative, Paranthropus robustus, lived there too. It grew bigger teeth for crushing tough food. Lead researcher Jesse Martin said this relative once outnumbered Homo erectus by more than 10 to one!
why_it_matters: Fossils like these help answer a big question kids often ask: where did people come from?
